nodes.label: examples workflow
nodes.rationale: Two jobs answering two questions: do the eight bundled example frontends still install and build (#903), and do the standalone examples still run (#545). src/** is in the path filter because of the snippets job and is the whole point of it - an examples-only filter would produce zero checks for exactly the failure this gate exists to catch. Before it, no workflow carried examples/** at all, so a PR touching only examples produced an empty check rollup (#890).

nodes.label: Example frontend install+build matrix
nodes.rationale: Eight explicitly listed directories (chat and voice, each angular/next/react/svelte) on Node 24 with fail-fast: false, so an Angular-only regression does not mask a Next-only one. npm ci deliberately, not npm install: only ci treats a desynced lockfile as an error rather than quietly rewriting it - ts-pattern was declared in six example manifests and missing from all six lockfiles, so npm ci failed in every example frontend on develop and nothing noticed. Listed rather than globbed so a new frontend is a deliberate line in the file. Node 24 is also load-bearing: @angular/cli 22 requires 24.15 or newer.

nodes.label: Standalone example runner job
nodes.rationale: Until #545 nothing in CI ever executed an example - a framework change could break every snippet in the tree and the only signal would be a user running one. tests/examples/examples.manifest.json classifies all 78 standalone scripts as runnable-with-an-assertion or skipped-with-a-reason, and the runner fails when manifest and tree disagree in either direction, so a new example cannot silently opt out. Bun only and deliberately so: the cross-runtime question belongs to bun run smoke, whose cases are runtime-neutral, while the examples reach for Bun.sleep and import .ts directly. timeout-minutes: 15 over ~90 s of work so a snippet that learns to hang goes red instead of burning six hours.

nodes.label: No rebuild-and-diff of committed bundles
nodes.rationale: Not a judgement call - for four of the original six legs it is impossible, measured by comparing two builds from an identical tree. Next mints a fresh build id per run, renaming the build-id directory and rewriting every RSC payload and HTML entry; Svelte writes a build timestamp into _app/version.json which index.html embeds; only Angular was byte-identical. A rebuild-and-diff gate would be permanently red on four legs regardless of staleness - the same conclusion check:ui reached for UiAssets.ts by a different route. A content-independent source-hash freshness gate is the open question in #903.
